Instead it was someone bludgeoning songs of the 60s and 70s into submission to a pre-recorded backing track. This led me to explain to my husband that ‘Anyone Who Had A Heart’ was originally recorded by Dion Warwick before it was a a huge UK hit for Cilla ‘Human Foghorn’ Black. When we got home we did a compare and contrast of a few versions. Dion’s original is lovely, but, as was usually the case, Dusty’s version is unsurpassable. Cilla’s is every bit as unsubtle as I recalled…

record.bridgyOriginalText: You know what is the saddest thing about the rise of LLM/GenerativeAI? That it, and the frequently (but not always) poor quality output it generates, have become the public perception of AI. All the incredible breakthroughs in Machine Learning, which has been transformative in many areas, is tarred with the brush of AI slop…. It isn’t like GAI/LLM don’t have its place (as tools for processing large datasets for example) but, as always, rampant capitalism has turned it into something morally compromised. I also think all the resources being used on GAI/LLM are ultimately wasted as the limits of the technology are becoming clear…

record.bridgyOriginalText: On Thursday I went to lunch with a salesman for a company we’ve just bought something from. We went to the cafe in the Weston Library in Oxford where they currently have an exhibition called ‘Pets and their People’ with various artefacts showing the history of man’s relationship with companion animals. One of the artefacts was a leather ‘pup mask’. The legend underneath explained, demurely, that some people like to dress up and behave like pets. ‘I don’t understand, who would wear something like that?’ he asked. I, being the very model of professional self-restraint, kept quiet. Though I did think ‘oh you sweet summer child’ (he was too young to have ever seen a Tamagotchi before)…
